title: Han2024 – SSVEP fatigue dataset with two frequency paradigms
description: A 64-channel EEG dataset from 24 healthy subjects performing steady-state visually evoked potential (SSVEP) brain-computer interface tasks across two frequency paradigms (8.0-15.5 Hz and 25.5-33.0 Hz). The dataset includes training and fatigue-state recordings to investigate the effects of mental fatigue on SSVEP-BCI performance using dynamic stopping strategies. Data were collected at 1000 Hz using JFPM encoding with 32 visual targets in a 4×4 matrix layout.
methods_description: EEG was recorded from 24 healthy subjects (12 male, 12 female, aged 18-26) using a 64-channel Synamps2 system (Neuroscan) at 1000 Hz sampling rate with Cz reference. Subjects performed two SSVEP-BCI paradigms: low-frequency (16 targets, 8.0-15.5 Hz, 0.5 Hz step) and high-frequency (16 targets, 25.5-33.0 Hz, 0.5 Hz step). Each paradigm used JFPM encoding with phase cycling (0, 0.5π, π, 1.5π) in a 4×4 matrix layout. The experiment consisted of training (6 blocks per condition) and fatigue (24 blocks per condition) phases, with each block containing 16 trials of 2-second stimulation. Data were epoched to 3-second windows (3000 samples) and preprocessed with online bandpass filtering (0.15-200 Hz).
